tiles.label: Go / no-go gates
tiles.sub: Gate 1: model acc ≥ 80% & DF ≤ 5%. Gate 2: model-only ≤ 10% & rescue (and clinician accuracy on AI-wrong cases) retained ≥ 50%; illustrative site thresholds

figures.title: Where do the two readers fail: on the same cases or on different ones?
figures.caption: The paper's paired 2x2 per workflow. Orange = model-only error (substitution risk), blue = clinician-only error (rescue potential), dark = shared error (common-mode failure). DF = double-fault rate; Q = Yule's Q.

figures.title: Does independence survive once one reader sees the other's answer?
figures.caption: Left: on cases where the shown answer was wrong, how often the second reader gave that same wrong answer when blind vs after seeing it. Right: double-fault rate per workflow with 95% Wilson CI; the orange tick is what independence would give.

figures.title: Does the answer change with case mix?
figures.caption: Per-stratum accuracy and double-fault rate (question type parsed from the stem). Strata that pass Gate 1 are the candidates for partial deployment; with ~12 cases each these are illustrations, not estimates.

figures.title: Why accuracy alone cannot answer the question
figures.caption: Left: three hypothetical models, all 90% accurate next to a 78%-accurate clinician, with minimum, independent and maximum overlap. Right: how many adjudicated cases it takes to pin the double-fault rate down.
